# `pattern-removed`

Pattern removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `pattern-removed` (both directions), `pattern-removed-in-request`, `pattern-removed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `pattern` was removed.

## Why this default

In requests: more values are valid. In responses: clients that parse values by the old pattern may fail.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  pattern-removed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the pattern in responses if clients rely on it.
